requirements.canonical: A definition made in the module definitions part outside of other scope units IS globally visible and MAY be used elsewhere in the module, including all functions, test cases and altsteps defined within the module.

requirements.original: Identifiers imported from other modules are also globally visible throughout the importing module.
requirements.canonical: An identifier imported from another module IS globally visible throughout the importing module.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 5.2.0 -- Identifiers imported from other modules are also globally visible throughout the importing module.

requirements.original: Definitions made in a test component type may be used in a component type extending this component type definition, and in functions, test cases and altsteps referencing that component type or a compatible test component type (see clause 6.3.2.7) by a runs on clause.
requirements.canonical: A definition made in a test component type MAY be used in a component type extending this component type.

requirements.original: Definitions made in a test component type may be used in a component type extending this component type definition, and in functions, test cases and altsteps referencing that component type or a compatible test component type (see clause 6.3.2.7) by a runs on clause.
requirements.canonical: A definition made in a test component type MAY be used in a function, test case or altstep that references that component type or a compatible test component type by a runs on clause.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 5.2.0 -- Definitions made in a test component type may be used in a component type extending this component type definition, and in functions, test cases and altsteps referencing that component type or a compatible test component type (see clause 6.3.2.7) by a runs on clause.

requirements.original: Test cases, altsteps and functions are individual scope units without any hierarchical relation between them, i.e. declarations made inside their body have local visibility and shall only be used in the given test case, altstep or function (e.g. a declaration made in a test case is not visible in a function called by the test case or in an altstep used by the test case).
requirements.canonical: Test cases, altsteps and functions ARE individual scope units without any hierarchical relation between them.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 5.2.0 -- Test cases, altsteps and functions are individual scope units without any hierarchical relation between them, i.e. declarations made inside their body have local visibility and shall only be used in the given test case, altstep or function (e.g. a declaration made in a test case is not visible in a function called by the test case or in an altstep used by the test case).

requirements.original: Test cases, altsteps and functions are individual scope units without any hierarchical relation between them, i.e. declarations made inside their body have local visibility and shall only be used in the given test case, altstep or function (e.g. a declaration made in a test case is not visible in a function called by the test case or in an altstep used by the test case).
requirements.canonical: A declaration made inside the body of a test case, altstep or function SHALL only be used in that test case, altstep or function.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 5.2.0 -- Test cases, altsteps and functions are individual scope units without any hierarchical relation between them, i.e. declarations made inside their body have local visibility and shall only be used in the given test case, altstep or function (e.g. a declaration made in a test case is not visible in a function called by the test case or in an altstep used by the test case).

requirements.original: Test cases, altsteps and functions are individual scope units without any hierarchical relation between them, i.e. declarations made inside their body have local visibility and shall only be used in the given test case, altstep or function (e.g. a declaration made in a test case is not visible in a function called by the test case or in an altstep used by the test case).
requirements.canonical: A declaration made in a test case IS NOT visible in a function called by the test case or in an altstep used by the test case.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 5.2.0 -- Test cases, altsteps and functions are individual scope units without any hierarchical relation between them, i.e. declarations made inside their body have local visibility and shall only be used in the given test case, altstep or function (e.g. a declaration made in a test case is not visible in a function called by the test case or in an altstep used by the test case).

requirements.original: Stand-alone statement blocks and statements within compound statements, like e.g. if-else, while, do-while, or `alt` statements may be used within test cases, altsteps, functions, or may be embedded in other statement blocks or compound statements, e.g. an if-else statement that is used within a while loop.
requirements.canonical: A stand-alone statement block or a compound statement (e.g. if-else, while, do-while, `alt`) MAY be used within test cases, altsteps and functions, or embedded in other statement blocks or compound statements.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 5.2.0 -- Stand-alone statement blocks and statements within compound statements, like e.g. if-else, while, do-while, or `alt` statements may be used within test cases, altsteps, functions, or may be embedded in other statement blocks or compound statements, e.g. an if-else statement that is used within a while loop.

requirements.original: Statement blocks and embedded statement blocks have a hierarchical relation both to the scope unit including the given statement block and to any embedded statement block.
requirements.canonical: A statement block IS hierarchically related both to the scope unit including it and to any statement block embedded in it.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 5.2.0 -- Statement blocks and embedded statement blocks have a hierarchical relation both to the scope unit including the given statement block and to any embedded statement block.

requirements.original: Declarations made within a statement block have local visibility.
requirements.canonical: A declaration made within a statement block has local visibility.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 5.2.0 -- Declarations made within a statement block have local visibility.

requirements.original: Declarations of a scope unit at a higher hierarchical level are visible in all units at lower levels within the same branch of the hierarchy.
requirements.canonical: A declaration of a scope unit at a higher hierarchical level IS visible in all units at lower levels within the same branch of the scope hierarchy.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 5.2.0 -- Declarations of a scope unit at a higher hierarchical level are visible in all units at lower levels within the same branch of the hierarchy.

requirements.original: Declarations of a scope unit in a lower level of hierarchy are not visible to those units at a higher hierarchical level.
requirements.canonical: A declaration of a scope unit at a lower hierarchical level IS NOT visible to units at a higher hierarchical level.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 5.2.0 -- Declarations of a scope unit in a lower level of hierarchy are not visible to those units at a higher hierarchical level.

requirements.canonical: The scope of a formal parameter of a parameterized object SHALL be restricted to the definition in which the formal parameter appears and to the lower levels of scope in the same scope hierarchy.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 5.2.1 -- The scope of formal parameters in a parameterized object (e.g. in a function definition) shall be restricted to the definition in which the parameters appear and to the lower levels of scope in the same scope hierarchy.

requirements.original: That is they follow the scope rules for local definitions (see clause 5.2).
requirements.canonical: A formal parameter follows the scope rules for local definitions.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 5.2.1 -- That is they follow the scope rules for local definitions (see clause 5.2).

requirements.original: TTCN-3 requires uniqueness of identifiers, i.e. all identifiers in the same scope hierarchy shall be distinctive.
requirements.canonical: All identifiers in the same scope hierarchy SHALL be distinctive.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 5.2.2 -- TTCN-3 requires uniqueness of identifiers, i.e. all identifiers in the same scope hierarchy shall be distinctive.

requirements.original: This means that a declaration in a lower level of scope shall not re-use the same identifier as a declaration in a higher level of scope in the same branch of the scope hierarchy.
requirements.canonical: A declaration in a lower level of scope SHALL NOT re-use the identifier of a declaration in a higher level of scope in the same branch of the scope hierarchy.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 5.2.2 -- This means that a declaration in a lower level of scope shall not re-use the same identifier as a declaration in a higher level of scope in the same branch of the scope hierarchy.

requirements.original: The identifier of a module (its module name) or of an imported module belongs to the scope unit of the module and cannot be used as identifier for other definitions inside this module.
requirements.canonical: The identifier of a module (its module name) or of an imported module belongs to the scope unit of the module.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 5.2.2 -- The identifier of a module (its module name) or of an imported module belongs to the scope unit of the module and cannot be used as identifier for other definitions inside this module.

requirements.original: The identifier of a module (its module name) or of an imported module belongs to the scope unit of the module and cannot be used as identifier for other definitions inside this module.
requirements.canonical: The name of a module or of a module imported into it SHALL NOT be used as identifier for other definitions inside this module.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 5.2.2 -- The identifier of a module (its module name) or of an imported module belongs to the scope unit of the module and cannot be used as identifier for other definitions inside this module.

requirements.original: Identifiers for fields of structured types, enumerated values and groups do not have to be globally unique, however in the case of enumerated values the identifiers, within the same module, they shall only be reused for enumerated values within other enumerated types or as identifiers for fields of structured types.
requirements.canonical: An identifier of a field of a structured type, of an enumerated value or of a group NEED NOT be globally unique.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 5.2.2 -- Identifiers for fields of structured types, enumerated values and groups do not have to be globally unique, however in the case of enumerated values the identifiers, within the same module, they shall only be reused for enumerated values within other enumerated types or as identifiers for fields of structured types.

requirements.original: Identifiers for fields of structured types, enumerated values and groups do not have to be globally unique, however in the case of enumerated values the identifiers, within the same module, they shall only be reused for enumerated values within other enumerated types or as identifiers for fields of structured types.
requirements.canonical: Within the same module, the identifier of an enumerated value SHALL only be reused for enumerated values within other enumerated types or as identifier of a field of a structured type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 5.2.2 -- Identifiers for fields of structured types, enumerated values and groups do not have to be globally unique, however in the case of enumerated values the identifiers, within the same module, they shall only be reused for enumerated values within other enumerated types or as identifiers for fields of structured types.

requirements.original: In addition, enumeration values shall not be used as names of value or template definitions of imported enumeration types, defining the given enumeration value (see also clause 8.2.3.1, example 5).
requirements.canonical: An enumerated value of an imported enumerated type SHALL NOT be used as the name of a value or template definition of that enumerated type.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence is hard to parse: it is unclear whether only value/template definitions of the imported enumerated type are restricted, or any value/template definition. The narrower reading (definitions of that type) was chosen as it matches "of imported enumeration types". The sentence also uses "enumeration value/type" instead of "enumerated value/type".
readings: An enumerated value of an imported enumerated type SHALL NOT be used as the name of a value or template definition of that enumerated type.
An enumerated value of an imported enumerated type SHALL NOT be used as the name of any value or template definition in the importing module.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 5.2.2 -- In addition, enumeration values shall not be used as names of value or template definitions of imported enumeration types, defining the given enumeration value (see also clause 8.2.3.1, example 5).

requirements.canonical: The rules of identifier uniqueness SHALL apply to identifiers of formal parameters.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 5.2.2 -- The rules of identifier uniqueness shall also apply to identifiers of formal parameters.

requirements.original: Generally, the order in which declarations can be made is arbitrary.
requirements.canonical: A declaration MAY be made in any order relative to other declarations, subject to the declaration-before-use rule for test case definitions, functions, altsteps and statement blocks.
requirements.condition: general case, except where clause 5.3 requires declaration before use

ambiguity.issue: "Generally" does not say where the arbitrary order applies; later sentences restrict it inside testcases, functions, altsteps and statement blocks. Chose the reading that the general rule is limited by those restrictions.
readings: A declaration MAY be made in any order anywhere, except that local definitions SHALL be declared before their first use.
A declaration MAY be made in any order only in the module definitions part and in a component type definition.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 5.3 -- Generally, the order in which declarations can be made is arbitrary.

requirements.original: Inside a statement block, such as a function body or a branch of an if-else statement, declarations (if any) can occur at any place where a statement can occur.
requirements.canonical: A declaration inside a statement block MAY occur at any place where a statement can occur.
requirements.condition: the declaration is inside a statement block (e.g. a function body or a branch of an if-else statement)
requirements.header: // @requirement: 5.3 -- Inside a statement block, such as a function body or a branch of an if-else statement, declarations (if any) can occur at any place where a statement can occur.

requirements.original: However inside test case definitions, functions, altsteps, and statement blocks, all required declarations shall be given before their first place of usage.
requirements.canonical: A declaration inside a testcase definition, function, altstep or statement block SHALL be given before its first place of usage.
requirements.condition: the declaration is inside a testcase definition, function, altstep or statement block

ambiguity.issue: "test case definitions" is used for the TTCN-3 testcase definition; the glossary term "test case" denotes the abstract test case, the language element is `testcase`.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 5.3 -- However inside test case definitions, functions, altsteps, and statement blocks, all required declarations shall be given before their first place of usage.

requirements.original: This means in particular, local variables, local timers, and local constants shall never be used before they are declared.
requirements.canonical: A local variable, local timer or local constant SHALL NOT be used before it is declared.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 5.3 -- This means in particular, local variables, local timers, and local constants shall never be used before they are declared.

requirements.original: The only exceptions to this rule are labels.
requirements.canonical: A label IS the only exception to the rule that declarations inside testcase definitions, functions, altsteps and statement blocks SHALL be given before their first place of usage.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 5.3 -- The only exceptions to this rule are labels.

requirements.original: Forward references to a label may be used in goto statements before the label occurs (see clause 19.8).
requirements.canonical: A `goto` statement MAY reference a label that occurs later in the same statement block (forward reference).
requirements.header: // @requirement: 5.3 -- Forward references to a label may be used in goto statements before the label occurs (see clause 19.8).
